checks: The actual final hand sorts factions and blueprints into a fixed visible order
Fifteen real cards render as four shop-style piles with exact counts
Sorting and stacking leave physical hand order, identities, score and all rule state untouched
Changing draw/order history does not change the visible faction/character order
An overwritten copy forms a separate worn pile instead of hiding under its original skill
Created cards stack only with equal costs and multipliers, separately from ordinary final prints
A newly created double-ability copy flies directly into its equivalent sorted pile without reserving an extra hand slot
A new created face reserves its final sorted position between factions instead of flying to the hand end
A render during the creation flight preserves that same sorted landing slot
A forced physical duplicate becomes the usable top card of its pile
An already selected physical copy remains the pile representative after a render
Three clicks on one pile select three distinct eligible payment cards and show the selected quantity
The actual payment limit still caps a stack selection
The minus control deselects one physical card without losing the pile or other selections
Double-click inspection restores the payment selection that existed before its first click
Finishing a payment removes all payment-only pile controls
Other modes retain their ordinary individual-card order and display
The real placement resolver plays exactly one chosen physical duplicate and leaves the other two in a counted pile with conserved inventory
Physical dragging lifts one clean card face while the source pile and actual hand remain intact
A real full faction collection activates matching background and foreground realms through the production UI hook
